Title: Diagnosis of test `testIsSameLocalTime_Cal`

Details: The test `testIsSameLocalTime_Cal` compares two `Calendar` objects using `DateUtils.isSameLocalTime` and expects that two times with different timezone offsets but the same local time components (e.g., 13:45:00 in GMT+1 vs 13:45:00 in GMT-1) should be considered the same local time.

The method `DateUtils.isSameLocalTime` compares specific fields of the two `Calendar` objects to determine if they represent the same local time. The fields checked are:

- MILLISECOND
- SECOND
- MINUTE
- HOUR (not HOUR_OF_DAY)
- DAY_OF_YEAR
- YEAR
- ERA
- The class type of the calendar objects

A key observation is that the method uses `Calendar.HOUR` instead of `Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY`. `Calendar.HOUR` represents the hour in 12-hour clock format (0-11), and `Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY` represents the hour in 24-hour format (0-23).

This causes an error when comparing times in the afternoon (hours 12 to 23) because `Calendar.HOUR` does not differentiate between AM and PM, leading to incorrect equality results.

For example, in the failing test, the two `Calendar` instances `cal3` and `cal4` are set to 4:00 and 16:00 respectively. `Calendar.HOUR` for 16:00 would be 4 (4 PM), and for 4:00 it would be 4 (4 AM), so the hours match. Because the other matching fields are the same, the method will consider the two times as the same local time mistakenly.

The use of `Calendar.HOUR` instead of `Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY` is thus the cause of the failure.

Suggested fix: Replace `Calendar.HOUR` with `Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY` in the `isSameLocalTime` method to accurately compare hours on a 24-hour basis.

Relevant lines from method `DateUtils.isSameLocalTime`:
```java
263 :                 cal1.get(Calendar.MINUTE) == cal2.get(Calendar.MINUTE) &&
264 :                 cal1.get(Calendar.HOUR) == cal2.get(Calendar.HOUR) &&
265 :                 cal1.get(Calendar.DAY_OF_YEAR) == cal2.get(Calendar.DAY_OF_YEAR) &&
```

Should instead use:
```java
264 :                 cal1.get(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY) == cal2.get(Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY) &&
```

This will fix the faulty comparison and make the test pass.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
